turns.speaker: user
turns.text: It's finally Friday and I have absolutely nothing planned.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Lovely feeling. Do you want a lazy weekend at home to recharge, or would you like to get out and do something?

contexts.pending: a lazy weekend at home or going out
think_reask: So, a lazy weekend at home, or getting out and about?
Time's up. Rest and recharge, or go do something?
welcome_back: Welcome back. We were planning your weekend, staying in or going out?
Hi again. Have you decided what kind of weekend you want?

endings.user: Home. I've been running around all week.
endings.moshi: You've earned it. Maybe plan one nice meal so it still feels special.

endings.user: Out, definitely. I'll go stir crazy otherwise.
endings.moshi: Great. There's a street market on Saturday morning that might be fun.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My parents are visiting on Saturday and I need to keep them entertained.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Nice. Would they enjoy something cultural like a museum, or something outdoors like a garden or a boat trip?

contexts.pending: a museum or something outdoors for the parents

Okay, what do you think they'd like more, culture or fresh air?
welcome_back: Welcome back. You were planning Saturday with your parents, museum or outdoors?
There you are. Did you pick something for your parents' visit?

endings.user: Outdoors. My dad can't sit still in museums.
endings.moshi: Then a boat trip could be perfect. Book in the morning before it gets crowded.

endings.user: Museum. My mum loves old paintings.
endings.moshi: Lovely. Check if there's a guided tour, they're often free on weekends.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Two different friends invited me to things on Saturday night.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Popular weekend. Is it a choice between a big party and something smaller, or are they both similar?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: One's a birthday party, the other is a quiet dinner.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Got it. Which one would you be more disappointed to miss?

contexts.pending: the birthday party or the quiet dinner

Okay, time's up. Birthday party or quiet dinner?
welcome_back: Welcome back. You were choosing between the party and the dinner on Saturday.
Hi again. Any closer to deciding between the two invitations?

endings.user: The dinner. I barely get to see that friend.
endings.moshi: Then go to the dinner and send a nice message to the birthday person.

endings.user: The party. It's her thirtieth, I can't miss that.
endings.moshi: Fair. Maybe suggest a different night for dinner with your other friend.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: {friend}, are you free on Sunday?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: In the afternoon, yeah. Morning I've got football.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: There's a food festival in the park. Want to go?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Oh, the one with the dumplings? I went last year, it was amazing.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: That's the one. Around two?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Two's perfect. I'll come hungry.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Did you book the cinema for Saturday?

turns.speaker: friend
turns.text: Not yet. I wasn't sure which film you wanted.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I don't mind. Anything but horror.

turns.text: Fine by me. What time does it start?

turns.text: Seven, so we can eat after.

turns.text: Booking it now.

turns.text: Are we still going to your sister's on Saturday?

turns.text: Oh no, poor thing. So we're free all day then?

turns.text: Or we could not do that and go for a long lunch instead.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Give me some ideas for a rainy Saturday with two kids.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: You could build a blanket fort and have a movie afternoon, or bake cookies together. Indoor swimming pools are great too, kids burn off energy.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Swimming is good. What else could we do out of the house?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: A science museum or an indoor climbing wall are both fun. Many libraries also run free story sessions on Saturday mornings.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The climbing wall sounds fun. Are kids / allowed at those?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Most have kids sessions, usually from about age five. It's best to book ahead, they fill up on rainy days.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Mine are six and eight, so perfect.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Great ages for it. Pack some snacks, they'll be starving afterwards.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I want to do something nice for my wife this weekend but I'm on a tight budget.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Lots of options. A picnic in a nice spot, cooking her favourite meal, or a sunset walk somewhere scenic are all lovely and cheap.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: She loves Italian food. Maybe I could / make her lasagna.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's a great idea. Make it in the afternoon, then it's ready when she gets home.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I've never made lasagna before though.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It's more forgiving than it looks. Use a simple meat sauce, layer it with pasta sheets and a white sauce, and bake for about forty minutes.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay. And maybe some candles.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Candles and a nice playlist, and you've got a proper date night at home.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm thinking of doing a little day trip on Sunday. Somewhere I can get to by train.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sounds fun. Do you prefer the seaside, a historic town, or countryside walks?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Seaside, I think. I haven't seen the sea in ages.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then pick a coastal town within about two hours by train. Leave early so you get a full day there.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What if the weather's bad?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Seaside towns are still nice in grey weather. A cozy cafe, the pier, maybe an aquarium if there's one.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Actually, I might / bring my sister along.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Even better. Check if there's a two together railcard or group ticket, it can save you a lot.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I always waste my weekends. How do people actually get stuff done?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: One trick is to pick just one or two things you really want to do, and leave the rest of the time free.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Only two? That seems like nothing.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It's enough. Most people try to cram in ten and end up doing none of them.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Fair. This weekend I want to / finally sort out my wardrobe.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Great. Do it Saturday morning while you've got energy, then you'll have the rest of the weekend to relax.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And the second thing could be seeing a friend.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Perfect balance, one chore and one treat. You'll feel like you had a real weekend.
